paper_metadata.title: Influence of HIP processing on microstructure and mechanical properties of superalloy Udimet 720LI

evidence.quote: Udimet 720LI (U720LI), is one of the nickel based superalloys primarily strengthened by c9 [Ni 3 (Ti, Al)] used for advanced aeroengine applications.
Mo 3 .0
Al 2 .2
Oxygen, ppm 140
Ni Balance
Inert gas atomised superalloy U720LI powder of size ,150 mm used in the present study was chemically analysed for its composition and oxygen content in the as received condition (Table 1).
Inert gas atomised powder with its composition conforming to that of the wrought nickel based superalloy U720LI was consolidated under optimised condition of hipping at 1200 uC/120 MPa/3 h.

samples.material_state: HIP + heat treated (solution treated and duplex aged)

evidence.quote: In order to improve the strength, the hipped alloy was subjected to a heat treatment consisting of solution treatment followed by two-step aging.
Inert gas (high purity argon) atomised powder of composition conforming to that of the superalloy Udimet 720 of low interstitial grade was hipped at 1200 uC/120 MPa/3 h.

other.capsule: stainless steel, 110 mm diameter, 2 mm wall thickness, 100 mm height

evidence.quote: The powder filled capsules were evacuated at room temperature (RT) and degassed at 800 uC for 8 h before crimp sealing under a dynamic vacuum of 6 ?5610 24 Pa.
The encapsulated powder was consolidated in an ASEA Quintus QIH-32 HIP at 1200 uC under a pressure of 120 MPa for 3 h.

parameters.cooling_method: oil quenched to RT (~120 uC min-1)

evidence.quote: A set of as hipped compacts were solution treated at 1100 uC for 2 h and oil quenched to RT, which was found to result in a cooling rate of ,120uC min 21.
These compacts were subsequently given an aging treatment at 650 uC for 24 h and air cooled followed by a second step aging treatment at 760uC for 16 h and air cooled.
